title: Lior and the Songbook
premise: Sable Thornbury's failing café survives on catering gigs, so when he's hired to bake for the Harrowgate Winter Music Festival, he can't refuse—even though the festival honors the estate of the late folk legend Maren Vale, whose songbook inheritance has split her two protégés into bitter rivals: Sable himself, once Maren's unofficial adopted son before he fled music for pastry, and Juniper Ashe, her polished official heir. A snowstorm traps Sable, Juniper, and Wren Calloway—Maren's estranged daughter and the 'best mistake' of both men's twenties—in the estate's guesthouse with the contested songbook, forcing three people who've spent a decade avoiding each other to finally read what Maren left behind. As the pages reveal that Maren willed not the songs but the choice itself to whoever truly sees her family whole, Sable must decide between the pastry career that saved him from grief and Wren, who finally sees him clearly—and he chooses Wren, singing one last song as the festival ends.
about_author: Rafael Lockridge is a former line cook turned novelist who writes love stories set in kitchens, concert halls, and the spaces where ambition meets tenderness. He lives in a snowy mountain town with his partner and an opinionated cat named Brioche.

chapters.title: Three Missed Payments
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Opening in the Flour Ghost café at dawn, Sable counts overdue invoices while hiding a framed photo of his younger self holding a guitar. The bank letter arrives; a festival catering contract offers exactly enough to survive. Emotional beat: quiet desperation masked by competence.

chapters.title: The Contract with Claws
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Reading the fine print, Sable learns the client is the Vale Estate—and the festival's artistic director is Juniper Ashe, his old rival. He signs anyway, telling himself ten years is long enough for anyone to be a stranger. Emotional beat: dread swallowed by necessity.

chapters.title: Juniper, Perfect as Ever
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper rehearses the tribute concert, resenting that Maren's will remains sealed and that the estate keeps hiring 'charity cases.' Spotting Sable's name on the vendor list, Juniper feels old humiliation spark fresh. Emotional beat: polished envy cracking into something rawer.

chapters.title: Wren Comes Home
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Maren's daughter returns to Harrowgate Estate for the first time since the funeral, tasked with opening the songbook vault at the festival's close. She hasn't spoken to either protégé since the night everything broke. Emotional beat: grief worn as armor.

chapters.title: Sugar Work and Old Wounds
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Setting up his pastry station on the estate, Sable collides—literally—with Wren carrying boxes of Maren's papers. Ten years collapse in a flour-dusted handshake neither lets go of quickly. Emotional beat: the past arriving without permission.

chapters.title: The Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Forecasts turn ugly; Juniper tries to move the tribute indoors and finds the estate manager has already left, locking the guesthouse keys in Juniper's pocket. A power flicker kills the road crews' signal. Emotional beat: control slipping through capable fingers.

chapters.title: Snowbound
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The storm hits early. Sable, mid-delivery, is stranded; Juniper shelters him in the guesthouse where Wren is cataloguing Maren's papers. Three people, one fire, forty-eight hours minimum. Emotional beat: trapped intimacy, doors closing on escape routes.

chapters.title: The Best Mistake
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Over emergency rations and Sable's rescued pastries, the history surfaces: the summer all three were inseparable, and the betrayal—the night Sable quit music and Wren left without goodbye—that each blames on the others. Emotional beat: bitterness curdling into confession.

chapters.title: What Maren Left Unfinished
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Sorting papers by lamplight, Wren finds an unrecorded song in Maren's handwriting, addressed to no one—or possibly to everyone. Juniper claims it belongs to the tribute; Sable recognizes the melody from a private lesson. Emotional beat: inheritance revealed as a question, not an answer.

chapters.title: Two Rivals, One Kitchen
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper commandeers Sable's portable oven to feed the stranded road crew, and the two rivals cook side by side, trading barbs that soften into the old rhythm of collaboration. Emotional beat: rivalry revealing itself as unfinished friendship.

chapters.title: The Songbook Vault
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Wren, against protocol, opens the vault early to keep the papers safe from cold damp. Inside: decades of journals naming Sable as 'the son I chose' and Juniper as 'the heir I made.' Neither was told. Emotional beat: shock reframing a decade of resentment.

chapters.title: Power Plays by Firelight
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Cornered by the journals, Juniper considers hiding the page naming Sable—Maren's legacy, the festival, the career built on being chosen. The temptation lasts one long night. Emotional beat: corruption offered and almost accepted.

chapters.title: Confession at 3 A.M.
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren admits she left because she couldn't watch Sable shrink himself to fit Maren's shadow—and that she loved him too much to be the reason he stayed small. Sable reveals he quit music believing Wren chose Juniper's world over him. Emotional beat: the misunderstanding that cost ten years, finally named.

chapters.title: Bread and Reckoning
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Baking through the night for the crew, Sable tells Wren about the café, the debt, the way pastry saved him when music felt like drowning. For the first time someone sees both halves of him without flinching. Emotional beat: being fully witnessed.

chapters.title: Juniper's Empty Page
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper burns nothing but drafts a speech claiming the unfinished song, then reads Maren's journal entry about 'giving my children the fight they needed to find each other.' The realization lands: even the rivalry may have been Maren's design. Emotional beat: rage at a dead woman's chess game.

chapters.title: The Road Opens
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Plows clear the pass; the festival resumes in twelve hours and the guesthouse spell breaks. Wren asks Sable to stay through the weekend—not as staff, as family. Sable hesitates, contract and café pulling him back. Emotional beat: freedom returning as a harder choice than captivity.

chapters.title: Terms of Inheritance
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Back at the main house, Juniper confronts the estate lawyers and discovers the will's final clause: the songbook goes to whoever the three of them jointly agree 'carries Maren whole.' Any two can outvote the third—but only unanimous consent unlocks the vault permanently. Emotional beat: power restructured into trust or stalemate.

chapters.title: The Festival Begins Again
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The tribute concert opens with Juniper performing flawlessly while Sable works the concession tent, watching the life he abandoned from behind a pastry case. Wren stands in the crowd looking only at him. Emotional beat: longing sharpened by proximity.

chapters.title: Climax: The Unfinished Song
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. At the vault-opening ceremony, Juniper does the unthinkable—hands the unfinished song to Sable and Wren together, publicly renouncing sole claim. But the vault mechanism fails, the lawyers threaten litigation, and Sable must sing the song from memory—the private lesson Maren gave him—to prove the inheritance real. Emotional beat: everything risked in four minutes of music.

chapters.title: What Sable Chooses
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The song works; the vault opens; the songbook passes to all three names. Then the offer Sable feared arrives: a touring residency that would save the café forever—if he leaves the valley immediately. He looks at Wren, at the found family assembled in the snow, and declines. Emotional beat: choosing people over rescue.

chapters.title: Flour Ghost, Second Verse
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Epilogue-adjacent: Juniper invests in the café—repaying an old debt of silence—and takes over the festival permanently, transformed from gatekeeper to host. Watching Sable and Wren hang Maren's portrait above the ovens, Juniper finally feels chosen too. Emotional beat: rivalry resolved into kinship.

chapters.title: The Songbook Stays Open
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. One year later: the café hosts a monthly song circle where the songbook lies open on the counter, anyone welcome to add a page. Sable bakes, Wren writes, and the last lines echo Maren's final note: legacies are living things. Emotional beat: warmth, continuity, and home at last.
